questions.q: Which specific Section of Rule V defines fire zones as areas where building construction is permitted based on occupancy, construction type, and fire resistance?
questions.n: Section 501 serves as the 'Fire Zones Defined' section, establishing the foundational parameters for zoning.

questions.q: Under Section 504, what is the specific requirement for erecting construction sheds or canopies in a fire zone?
o: No permit is needed if they are temporary
A special permit from the Building Official
questions.n: Section 504.1 mandates a special permit for temporary buildings used for public protection or construction work.

questions.q: Which Section should you reference if you need to determine the classification of a building that sits on the boundary of two different fire zones?
questions.n: Section 502, 'Buildings Located in More Than One Fire Zone', provides the 1/3 area rule for classification.

questions.q: According to Section 507, which zone allows for exterior walls with only 'one-hour fire-resistivity throughout'?
questions.n: Section 507 describes suburban areas in these zones as permitted to have at least one-hour fire-resistivity throughout.

questions.q: Section 505 mandates that distances from the street center line must be measured in what specific way?
o: Along the curve of the sidewalk
At right angles to the street or alley
questions.n: Section 505 explicitly requires measurements to be at right angles to the street or alley.

questions.q: If an existing building in a fire zone does not comply with new rules, which Section prohibits its future enlargement?
questions.n: Section 506, 'Restrictions on Existing Buildings', prohibits the enlargement of non-compliant structures.

questions.q: Under Section 503, the requirements for moved buildings also explicitly apply to which other type of construction?
questions.n: Section 503.2 states that rules for moved buildings also apply to pre-engineered/pre-fabricated structures.

questions.q: Section 507 describes 'Highly Fire Restrictive Zones' as requiring exterior walls of at least how many hours fire-resistivity?
questions.n: Section 507 specifies that Highly Fire Restrictive Zones require three to four-hour resistivity, including exterior walls.

questions.q: Which Section allows the LGU to designate fire zones through the enactment of local ordinances?
questions.n: Section 507, 'Designation of Fire Zones', gives the legislative body of the LGU the power to enact these ordinances.

questions.q: According to Section 507, what type of construction is typical for 'Non-Fire Restricted Zones'?
questions.n: Section 507 notes that Non-Fire Restricted Zones may cluster dwellings of indigenous materials up to Types I and II construction.

questions.q: Which specific Section of Rule V should you consult to understand the general definition of Fire Zones based on occupancy and construction type?
questions.n: Section 501 serves as the introductory section where fire zones are officially defined for the code.

questions.q: Under Section 504, what is the mandatory requirement for erecting a temporary construction shed in a fire zone?
o: A special permit from the Building Official
No permit is required if removed within 60 days
A public ordinance from the LGU
A clearance from the Fire Marshall only
questions.n: Section 504.1 requires a special permit for temporary buildings like sheds or stands to ensure public safety in fire zones.

questions.q: According to Section 502, if a building is located such that exactly 40% of its area is in a Highly Fire Restrictive Zone, which rules must it follow?
o: The rules of the Highly Fire Restrictive Zone
A customized blend of both zone requirements
The rules of the less restrictive zone
questions.n: Section 502 mandates following the stricter zone if more than one-third (33.3%) of the area is within it; 40% exceeds this threshold.

questions.q: Which Section of Rule V describes the 'Center Lines of Streets' and how they function as property boundaries?
questions.n: Section 505 explicitly defines street center lines as the baseline for measuring distances to property lines.

questions.q: Section 506.1 prohibits what action regarding non-compliant existing buildings in fire zones?
o: They cannot be occupied by more than 10 people.
They must be demolished within 10 years.
They must be painted with fire-retardant paint annually.
They shall not hereafter be enlarged.
questions.n: Section 506 prevents the expansion of fire-risk by prohibiting the enlargement of non-compliant structures.

questions.q: Which specific entity does Section 507 grant the power to designate fire zones through local ordinances?
o: The Legislative Body of the LGU
The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture
questions.n: Section 507 identifies the local legislative body (like the Sanggunian) as the authority for enacting zoning ordinances.

questions.q: Under Section 507, buildings in a 'Fire Restrictive Zone' are generally required to have exterior walls with at least how many hours of fire-resistivity?
questions.n: Section 507 specifies that Fire Restrictive Zones require exterior walls of at least two-hour fire-resistivity.

questions.q: What construction types are typically clustered in 'Non-Fire Restricted Zones' according to Section 507?
questions.n: Section 507 notes that non-restricted zones usually permit dwellings of indigenous materials and Types I and II construction.

questions.q: Section 503.2 specifies that the rules for 'Moved Buildings' also apply to which of the following?
questions.n: Section 503.2 explicitly links moved buildings to those that are dismantled and re-assembled (pre-fab).

questions.q: In Highly Fire Restrictive Zones, Section 507 requires building materials to have a fire-resistive rating of no less than:
questions.n: Highly Fire Restrictive Zones require the maximum protection tier of 3 to 4 hours.
